    24	==================================
    25	Accessing Online Astronomical Data
    26	==================================
    27	
    28	Astroquery is an `astropy <https://www.astropy.org>`_ affiliated package that
    29	contains a collection of tools to access online Astronomical data. Each web
    30	service has its own sub-package. For example, to interface with the `SIMBAD
    31	website <https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/>`_, use the ``simbad`` sub-package:
    32	
    33	.. code-block:: python
    34	
    35	    >>> from astroquery.simbad import Simbad
    36	    >>> theta1c = Simbad.query_object('tet01 Ori C')
    37	    >>> theta1c.pprint()
    38	       main_id          ra           dec      ... coo_wavelength     coo_bibcode       matched_id 
    39	                       deg           deg      ...                                                 
    40	    ------------- ------------- ------------- ... -------------- ------------------- -------------
    41	    * tet01 Ori C 83.8186095697 -5.3897005033 ...              O 2020yCat.1350....0G * tet01 Ori C
    42	
    43	Installation and Requirements
    44	-----------------------------
    45	
    46	Astroquery works with Python 3.7 or later.
    47	As an `astropy`_ affiliate, astroquery requires `astropy`_ version 4.2.1 or later.
    48	
    49	astroquery uses the `requests <https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>`_
    50	module to communicate with the internet.  `BeautifulSoup
    51	<https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/>`_ and `html5lib'
    52	<https://html5lib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/>`_ are needed for HTML parsing for
    53	some services.  The `keyring <https://pypi.python.org/pypi/keyring>`_ module is
    54	also required for accessing services that require a login.  These can all be
    55	installed using `pip <https://pypi.python.org/pypi/pip>`_ or `anaconda
    56	<https://www.anaconda.com/>`_.  Running the tests requires `curl
    57	<https://curl.haxx.se/>`_ to be installed.
    58	
    59	The latest version of astroquery can be pip installed (note the ``--pre`` for
    60	picking up released developer versions, and ``-U`` for upgrade):
    61	
    62	.. code-block:: bash
    63	
    64	    $ python -m pip install -U --pre astroquery
    65	
    66	To install all the mandatory and optional dependencies add the ``[all]``
    67	identifier to the pip command above (or use ``[docs]`` or ``[test]`` for the
    68	dependencies required to build the documentation or run the tests):
    69	
    70	.. code-block:: bash
    71	
    72	    $ python -m pip install -U --pre astroquery[all]
    73	
    74	
    75	To install the 'bleeding edge' version:
    76	
    77	.. code-block:: bash
    78	
    79	   $ python -m pip install git+https://github.com/astropy/astroquery.git
    80	
    81	or cloned and installed from source:
    82	
    83	.. code-block:: bash
    84	
    85	    $ # If you have a github account:
    86	    $ git clone git@github.com:astropy/astroquery.git
    87	    $ # If you do not:
    88	    $ git clone https://github.com/astropy/astroquery.git
    89	    $ cd astroquery
    90	    $ python -m pip install .
    91	
    92	Using astroquery
    93	----------------
    94	
    95	Importing astroquery on its own doesn't get you much: you need to import each
    96	sub-module specifically.  See the documentation for a list of `Available
    97	Services <https://astroquery.readthedocs.io/en/latest/#available-services>`_.
    98	The `API`_ shows the standard suite of tools common to most modules, e.g.
    99	`query_object` and `query_region`.
   100	
   101	To report bugs and request features, please use the issue tracker.  Code
   102	contributions are very welcome, though we encourage you to follow the `API`_
   103	and `contributing guidelines
   104	<https://github.com/astropy/astroquery/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst>`_ as much
   105	as possible.
   106	
   107	Citing Astroquery
   108	-----------------
   109	
   110	If you use ``astroquery``, please cite the paper we published in `The
   111	Astronomical Journal <https://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157...98G>`__.
   112	
   113	The BibTeX entry is available from the package itself::
   114	
   115	  import astroquery
   116	  astroquery.__citation__
   117	
   118	
   119	In addition you may also want to refer to specific versions of the
   120	package. We create a separate Zenodo DOI for each version, they can be
   121	looked up at the following `Zenodo page <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.591669>`__
